title: 饮湖上初晴后雨
titlePy: Yǐn Hú Shàng Chū Qíng Hòu Yǔ
titleEn: Drinking on the Lake: Fine at First, Then Rain (No. 2)
author: 苏轼
intro: Sunshine or rain, Hangzhou’s West Lake is lovely — as lovely as the legendary beauty Xi Shi, whether she wears light make-up or heavy. This little poem is why West Lake is still called 西子湖.
analysis: 苏轼在杭州做官时，有一天在西湖上喝酒，先是晴天，后来下起雨来，他写了两首诗，这是第二首，也是最有名的一首。前两句写两种天气下的西湖：晴天时，阳光照在水面上，波光闪闪，最好看；下雨时，远处的山在雨雾中朦朦胧胧，也很奇妙。“晴方好”“雨亦奇”是一组对仗（两句字数相同、意思相对）。后两句用了一个比喻：如果把西湖比作古代美女西施，那么不管她化淡妆还是浓妆，都一样美。这个比喻很巧：晴天像浓妆，雨天像淡妆，西湖怎么样都美。从此西湖有了一个别名叫“西子湖”。
analysisEn: While serving as an official in Hangzhou, Su Shi went drinking on West Lake one day. It was sunny at first, then it began to rain, and he wrote two short poems about it. This is the second and far more famous one. The first two lines show the lake in both kinds of weather. In sunshine the water ripples and sparkles — it looks its best. In rain the hills around it fade into mist — and that is wonderful too. These two lines mirror each other word for word (水光 / 山色, 晴 / 雨, 好 / 奇), a technique called duìzhàng, or parallelism. Then comes the comparison everyone remembers: if you liken West Lake to Xi Shi, the most famous beauty of ancient China, then whether she wears light make-up or heavy, she always looks just right. The sunny lake is the bright, made-up face; the rainy lake is the soft, natural one. Since this poem, West Lake has had a second name, 西子湖, “Lake Xizi”. If you visit Hangzhou, you will see the poem everywhere.
background: Su Shi (1037–1101) served as vice-prefect of Hangzhou from 1071 to 1074, and this poem is traditionally dated to 1073. He later returned as prefect and built the causeway across the lake still called the Su Causeway (苏堤).
pronunciation: 潋滟 liàn yàn。空蒙 kōng méng。浓抹 mǒ。相宜 xiāng yí。西子 xī zǐ。
version: 采用统编小学语文教材（三年级上册）版本，作“空蒙”；一作“空濛”。原题共两首，本篇为第二首。

lines.py: shuǐ guāng liàn yàn qíng fāng hǎo
lines.lit: The water’s light ripples and sparkles — in sunshine it is just right;
lines.en: Sun on the water, rippling and glittering — the lake is at its best in fine weather;

lines.py: shān sè kōng méng yǔ yì qí
lines.lit: the hills’ colour hazy and misty — in rain it is also wonderful.
lines.en: hills soft and hazy in the rain — and that is a marvel too.

lines.py: yù bǎ xī hú bǐ xī zǐ
lines.lit: If I want to compare West Lake to Xi Zi,
lines.en: If you compare West Lake to the beauty Xi Shi,

lines.py: dàn zhuāng nóng mǒ zǒng xiāng yí
lines.lit: light make-up or heavy paint, always suitable.
lines.en: light make-up or heavy, she always looks just right.

words.en: to want to; if one wants to
Xi Shi, the famous beauty of the Spring and Autumn period
words.note: 就是西施，中国古代四大美女之一。
今天仍用来形容不同的打扮或风格。

imagery.name: 水
imagery.zh: 晴天的湖水波光闪闪，是西湖最明亮的一面。
imagery.en: Sunlit water sparkling with ripples — West Lake at its brightest.

imagery.name: 山
imagery.zh: 雨中的山朦朦胧胧，是西湖柔和、神秘的一面。
imagery.en: Hills blurred by rain — the soft, mysterious side of the lake.

imagery.name: 雨
imagery.zh: 雨不扫兴，反而让西湖有另一种美，像美人的淡妆。
imagery.en: Rain doesn’t spoil the day; it gives the lake another kind of beauty, like a woman’s light make-up.

imagery.name: 西湖
imagery.zh: 西湖被比作美女西施，晴雨都美，从此有了“西子湖”的别名。
imagery.en: The lake is likened to the beauty Xi Shi — lovely in sun or rain — and has been called Lake Xizi ever since.
